content.text:
The pattern fits Ba₂La₂Ti₂Cu₂O₁₁ (mp-1214655) alone. I only simulated three of the nine candidates, so the other six were judged by eye, not against their simulations.

- **Observed peaks:** the strongest is near 32° (100). Medium peaks appear near 22.5°, 39.5°, 46° and 57°. Weaker ones are near 35.5°, 45.5°, 67° and 76°.
- **mp-1214655 (Ba₂La₂Ti₂Cu₂O₁₁):** its simulation puts a peak at every one of those spots. The relative heights roughly agree, including the pair of peaks near 45.5° and 46°.
- **mp-1188807 (Sr₂CaReO₆):** its simulation has a strong peak (41) near 18.5°. The observed data there are only noise, at about 12 or less, so it is ruled out.
- **mp-1284552 (Sr₂TaMnO₆):** its simulation has a strong peak (31) near 19.2°. The observed data there are also only noise, so it is ruled out.
- **The other six:** the observed pattern has few peaks, and Ba₂La₂Ti₂Cu₂O₁₁ accounts for all of them. That leaves no unexplained peak that would point to a second phase.
